t: Permissions and Claude Code parity: Consequences you should know
x: Consequences you should know Agent Office no longer blocks anything on its own. If your settings allow Read(**) or Bash broadly, an agent can read ~/.claude/agent-office/bridge.json . That is now harmless for approvals: the bridge key opens only /bridge/* (asking for a terminal decision and polling its own messages), and the key that decides approvals, hires and switches lives only in the Electron process memory and an HttpOnly cookie that agents cannot read. With the bridge key an agent could at most raise a prompt card or read messages queued for a terminal session; it cannot answer prompts,

Security model Local only, two separate credentials. The server binds 127.0.0.1 and rejects any other Host header (DNS rebinding). The terminal bridge key in bridge.json opens /bridge/* only. The UI key exists only in the Electron process and the server's memory and reaches the windows as an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, so an agent that can read bridge.json still cannot approve its own requests. Decisions also need a per-session nonce. Keys are compared by hash in constant time and never logged. Strict Content-Security-Policy. Pages load scripts, styles and fonts only from the app itself

Security notes The server is local only, requires a random key, checks the Host header and sends a strict Content-Security-Policy. Electron windows are sandboxed with context isolation and no Node integration. Installs and updates are https only and SHA-256 verified. Windows and macOS builds are unsigned. Full list in the README . Background work and memory Agent Office keeps its background work small. Two settings in kiro.json tune it: tiroIdleMinutes (default 15, 0 = never): Tiro's own claude process holds a few hundred MB while idle, so it is closed after this many idle minutes and resumed

The Security Guard is an extra layer that watches for the things an AI agent should not do quietly: sending your secrets off the computer, running a script someone else wrote, harvesting credentials, or acting on instructions hidden in a web page or an email. It is a safety net, not a boundary : it asks you first; it never decides for you.

t: Security Guard: What it is, and what it is not
x: What it is, and what it is not ask-only. A hook (a small check Claude Code runs before and after each tool call) can only answer "ask the user first" or say nothing. It never approves, never denies, never rewrites what a tool will do. Your own Claude Code permissions (allow, deny, ask rules, permission mode) stay in charge: a deny rule still denies, and the Guard cannot turn an ask into an allow. Where it runs. In every Agent Office session (Tiro and every agent it hires; the hooks fire for sub-agents too) and, through the bridge plugin, in your own Claude Code terminals ( bridge/hooks/guard-h

t: Troubleshooting: SmartScreen and Smart App Control
x: SmartScreen and Smart App Control The installer is not code-signed. Compare its SHA-256 with the one on the download page before you run it. SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC". If the SHA-256 matches, choose More info , then Run anyway . Smart App Control (Windows 11) can block an unsigned installer and offer no Run anyway option. It is a Windows setting under Windows Security, App and browser control, Smart App Control settings. Turning it off can be permanent on some Windows 11 versions, so decide deliberately. If you cannot accept that, do not install the unsigned build.

The dashboard, island and tools talk to a local HTTP API. Every call to /api/... is a POST with a JSON body, authenticated by the UI session cookie (there is no key in URLs or headers; the bridge key only opens /bridge/* ). Decision endpoints ( /api/decide , /api/hire/decide , /api/switch , /api/send , /api/task , /api/sops/save , /api/boss-reset ) also need the per-session nonce in the x-nonce header. Not signed in returns 401, a missing nonce 403, a wrong Host header 403. GET /api/stream is a Server-Sent Events feed of the live snapshot. The bridge plugin also uses /bridge/ask and /bridge/po

Collapsed: shows Tiro's eyes (idle, working, waiting for approval, done, offline). While music plays it widens to show the title, artist and a synced lyric line. Expanded (hover, click, Ctrl+Alt+K , or when an approval arrives): tabs Home, Calendar and Settings, a dock of quick actions (Today, Reports, Usage, Office, Chat, and others you pin), approval buttons (keys Y and N answer the first request, Esc waves it away), and a Now playing card
Tray The tray menu has: Open office, Show notch (checkbox), Island (mode, chime on approval or done, display choice), Show Tiro, Start with Windows (packaged app only) and Quit Agent Office.

API reference The dashboard, island and tools talk to a local HTTP API. Every call to /api/... is a POST with a JSON body, authenticated by the UI session cookie (there is no key in URLs or headers; the bridge key only opens /bridge/* ). Decision endpoints ( /api/decide , /api/hire/decide , /api/switch , /api/send , /api/task , /api/sops/save , /api/boss-reset ) also need the per-session nonce in the x-nonce header. Not signed in returns 401, a missing nonce 403, a wrong Host header 403. GET /api/stream is a Server-Sent Events feed of the live snapshot. The bridge plugin also uses /bridge/ask

FAQ Does the office cost tokens? No. Only agents working cost tokens, and only on your Claude Code plan. Can an agent hire without asking me? No. Every hire needs your one-shot approval. Where is my data? On your machine: ~/.claude/agent-office , your vault, and Claude Code's own ~/.claude/projects . Model calls go to Anthropic through Claude Code, as in the terminal. Does it read my email? No. The scheduler reads a local feed file that you must produce yourself. Can I rename agents and keep their history? Yes; history follows the type, not the name. Security notes The server is local only, requires a random key, checks the Host header and sends a strict Content-Security-Policy. Electron windows are sandboxed with context isolation and no Node integration. Installs and updates are https only and SHA-256 verified. Windows and macOS builds are unsigned. Full list in the README . Background work and memory Agent Office keeps its background work small. Two settings in kiro.json tune it: tiroIdleMinutes (default 15, 0 = never): Tiro's own claude process holds a few hundred MB while idle, so it is closed after this many idle minutes and resumed
